events.desc: Digital Delivery Chicago 📌 **AI Apps Don’t Fail Because of the Tech Alone - They Fail When People Don’t Adopt Them** with Andjelka Djukic A great demo gets attention. Getting people to use your AI product in their everyday work is a different challenge. Drawing on practical examples from SaaS, EdTech, and digital marketing, Andjelka Djukic explores where adoption breaks down: confusing onboarding, poor workflow fit, lack of trust, and the gaps between what teams build, sell, and users actually need. We’ll look at how product and development teams can spot these problems earlier and build adoption into delivery, with time for discussion and experiences from the room. Andjelka Djukic is Head of Sales and Marketing at Eclincher and Co-Founder of Innovative Women of Serbia. Her work across SaaS, education technology, and international business development gives her a close-up view of what happens when technology meets real working habits. With a background in education, she brings a perspective on learning, trust, and organizational culture to conversations about AI adoption. 📌 **Polling Is a Backstop, Not a Clock: Building High-Precision Durable Timers** with Oluwafemi Shobande Backend systems are full of timers: retries, TTLs, leases, scheduled jobs, sleeps. A common way to find what is due is to run a loop that wakes up on a fixed interval and checks the database. That ties precision and cost together. Poll more often and timers fire closer to their deadline, but every replica does more database work, even when nothing is happening. This talk is about breaking that link. The ideas are inspired by firm timers, first proposed for Linux in 2002, and by applying similar ideas at the application layer in Aiki, an open source durable workflow framework created by me. But the design applies to any service that needs to fire things on time. Oluwafemi is the creator of Aiki, an open-source durable execution framework. Before working on Aiki full-time, he was a senior engineer at Bolt, where he helped build the company's on-demand food and grocery delivery business from its early days. Previously, he worked on real-time audio and video infrastructure for Microsoft Teams and distributed ledger technology at Interswitch, Nigeria's first unicorn. 📌 **Confidence Is a Lie (and You Can Get Good at Telling It)** with Caren Young “Just be more confident” is useless advice. Attendees leave with things they can use in their next meeting, like “Know your outcome before you walk in the room” and “Get micro-yeses along the way.” Caren was Manager of Product Management at Pivotal Labs, then a senior PM at California’s Department of Health Care Services and a product ops lead at HHS, and she's now a product coach and consultant. She's sat in plenty of rooms where design, development, and delivery each thought the problem belonged to someone else. She's also a stage performer and producer (twelve years), which turns out to be an unreasonably good way to learn how to be heard when the people in the room aren't always fans. 📣 If you're interested in speaking at an upcoming meetup, please email Bennett at bhansen@bitovi.com.

events.host: Chicago AI, ML and Computer Vision
events.desc: Chicago AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision. **Time, Date and Location** Nov 11, 2026 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-november-11-2026)** **Agentic RAG: Beyond Retrieve-and-Generate** Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the default pattern for grounding large language models in external knowledge, but most implementations still follow a rigid retrieve-once, generate-once pipeline — one that struggles with multi-hop questions, ambiguous queries, and knowing when its own retrieved context is insufficient. This talk introduces Agentic RAG, where retrieval is treated as an action within an agent's reasoning loop rather than a fixed upstream step. We'll examine query decomposition and routing for breaking complex questions into targeted sub-queries, self-reflective and corrective retrieval loops that let an agent judge and re-query its own results, and tool-orchestration patterns (via MCP) that let retrieval sit alongside other agent actions like database lookups and API calls. Using a live architecture — evolving a standard RAG chatbot into an agentic, MCP-connected system — we'll walk through what changes in design, and where these systems introduce new failure modes: grounding drift, latency and cost from repeated retrieval loops, and cases where a simpler RAG pipeline still wins. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for deciding when the added complexity of agentic RAG is worth it, and a set of design patterns for building it correctly. *About the Speaker* [Balaji Venkatasubramaniyar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/balaji-venkatasubramaniyar/) is a Technical Lead at Wisdom Infotech, leading a 15+ person engineering team delivering enterprise solutions. With 13+ years of experience in enterprise software and insurance technology, he specializes in agentic AI systems, RAG architectures, and vector databases. **GeoAI for the Physical World: Earth Observation, Foundation Models, and Urban Digital Twins** Earth observation provides a unique form of computer vision for understanding the physical world at city to continental scales. In this talk, I will show how satellite imagery, geospatial data, machine learning, and foundation-model representations can be combined to characterize urban environments and environmental conditions. I will present UrbanScope Open, an open GeoAI digital-twin prototype integrating Earth observation with 3D buildings, vegetation, land-surface temperature, air quality, noise, population, and other urban data. I will also share lessons from my research using geospatial foundation-model embeddings for environmental prediction across Europe. The talk will discuss how these approaches can contribute to increasingly multimodal AI systems capable of reasoning about real-world environments. *About the Speaker* [Cesar Alvarez](https://voxel51.com/events/cesar.alvarez@uni-a.de) is a researcher at the University of Augsburg working at the intersection of GeoAI, Earth observation, remote sensing, and environmental intelligence. His research applies machine learning, computer vision, and geospatial foundation models to problems including urban environments, climate risk, air quality, and agriculture. **Can agents get curious?** Most AI agents are good at answering a question once we tell them exactly what to look for. The harder problem is building agents that can explore a complex dataset autonomously: generating hypotheses, deciding which analyses are worth running, allocating additional compute when evidence is ambiguous, and knowing when they have enough evidence to stop. In this talk, I’ll show an architecture for autonomous research agents that combines structured knowledge, iterative tool use, and explicit evidence tracking to turn open-ended questions into a sequence of testable investigations. I’ll discuss practical lessons from building and evaluating these systems, including why more test-time compute does not automatically produce better research and how provenance and evaluation can make long-running agents more reliable. I’ll close with a live example of an agent exploring a dataset, revising its hypotheses, and choosing what to investigate next. *About the Speaker* [Srivatsa P](https://www.linkedin.com/in/srivatsa-p) is a member of technical staff at Sigma Computing, where he works on AI agents that reason over complex enterprise data. Previously, he worked on machine learning at Apple and conducted research at the MIT Media Lab; outside of traditional ML, he has also worked on mapping coral reefs through underwater imaging, which sparked an enduring interest in how intelligent systems make sense of messy real-world data. **Does Cross-Validation Work in Deep Learning?** Cross-validation is a standard in hyperparameter optimization in classical ML, but is generally considered computationally prohibitive and unnecessary in deep learning. We investigated whether CV produces 1. better DL models 2. better estimates of future performance of said models. We focused on medical image classification as an important deep learning application domain. events.title: Nov 19 - Visualizing and Debugging Hugging Face's LeRobot Data
events.host: Chicago AI, ML and Computer Vision
events.desc: Chicago AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup This workshop is a hands-on tour of what actually breaks when you load real LeRobot datasets, and how Voxel51's native LeRobot support in FiftyOne catches it. **Date, Time and Location** Nov 19, 2026 9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/lerobot-workshop-november-19-2026)** Robot learning data doesn't look like the data that trains most vision-language models. It's temporal, low-dimensional in the parts that matter most, embodiment-specific, and expensive to collect, and increasingly, it's shipped in Hugging Face's LeRobot format. But packaging robot data consistently isn't the same as being able to see it: episodes hide broken metadata, silently dropped sensor modalities, and mismatched schemas between robots that look identical on paper. Starting from the core differences that make robot data hard (temporal structure, proprioception, action grounding, embodiment heterogeneity, data scarcity), we'll move into live debugging: a metadata bug that broke multiple dataset imports, sensor streams that vanish without an error, and two robots running an identical benchmark whose data is structurally incompatible. By the end, you'll know what to check before you trust a LeRobot dataset, and how to actually look inside one.

events.title: Dec 10 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
events.host: Chicago AI, ML and Computer Vision
events.desc: Chicago AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision. **Date, Time and Location** Dec 10, 2026 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-december-10-2026)** **Your mAP is fine. Your slices are not. Finding the images that actually matter** A single mAP can look acceptable while one slice is unusable, small objects, occlusion, or a confused class. I will run a pretrained detector on a few hundred public images (COCO-style, not a production crawl), report the headline metric, then break the same run by slice and walk through the worst samples. The claim is modest: you do not need a million images or a trained-from-scratch model to see what the mean is hiding, and you cannot relabel everything, so the next labeling budget should follow those slices. No employer data and no confidential dashboards. *About the Speaker* [Amandeep Jiddewar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amanfj/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Pinterest, with prior work in U.S. manufacturing analytics (CertainTeed / Saint-Gobain) and marketplace allocation (QuinStreet). Emory Goizueta MSBA (2019), Kaggle Expert. This talk is in his personal capacity and does not represent his current or prior employers. **Production AI Agents: Tool Use, Evaluation, Guardrails and Observability** Building an AI agent is easy. Knowing whether it is behaving reliably in production is much harder. This session explores how to evaluate agents that use tools and external systems, including tool-call validation, tracing, observability, failure analysis, guardrails, permissions, and human review. Attendees will learn practical patterns for understanding not just what an agent answered, but why it acted and whether the action was safe. *About the Speaker* [Akshay Talathi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/akshaytalathi/) is a Vice President at Goldman Sachs with over 10 years of experience building large-scale, cloud-native, and distributed systems across financial services and technology. His current focus is GenAI and agentic AI, including production AI agents, MCP, enterprise integrations, guardrails, observability, and reliable AI-driven workflows. **From Virtual Worlds to Physical AI: Building Simulation Pipelines That Survive the Real World** Robots are moving beyond perception systems that only detect and classify objects toward systems that must understand a scene, learn behaviors, and act in the physical world. In this talk, I’ll show a practical Physical AI workflow using OpenUSD, BowerBot, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to build a robot’s virtual world, including its body, cameras, sensors, and environment. We’ll explore how demonstrations and reinforcement learning can teach behaviors in simulation, how vision and sensor data become observations for a robot policy, and what needs to match when transferring that behavior to real hardware. The demo follows a small robot from a simulated environment toward a real-world task, exposing both the power and the limitations of sim-to-real. The goal is to make the path from pixels to actions concrete for computer vision and machine learning practitioners. *About the Speaker* [Arturo Morales Rangel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arturo-morales-rangel) is the founder of Binary Core LLC, a Physical AI engineering company working across simulation, perception, robot learning, and deployment. **Prompting Video-Language Models in Production: Lessons from Enterprise Video Tagging and Evaluation** Video-language models can now describe, tag and answer questions about long-form video, but production results depend heavily on prompt design and evaluation. This talk shares field lessons from deploying such models for media, news, streaming and sports organizations, including how to structure prompts for consistent, schema-bound outputs across hours of footage. On one sports video-tagging project, consolidating the prompt definitions cut estimated processing cost about 3x, and about 90% of the originally reported issues were later resolved through prompting alone. I'll also walk through building evaluation frameworks for video outputs, including for hard domains like egocentric video, and what changes when migrating between model versions. Attendees will leave with reusable prompt patterns and an evaluation checklist they can apply to their own video pipelines. *About the Speaker* [Yash Gugale](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yashgugale/) is a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at TwelveLabs in New York, integrating video foundation models (Marengo for embeddings and search, Pegasus for video-language understanding) for media, news, streaming and sports customers. He previously spent about six years in video streaming engineering at Peloton and Samsung TV Plus, and holds an MS in Computer Graphics Technology from Purdue.

events.title: IndyPy - Django & FastAPI: What's Next?
events.desc: AWS Chicago User Group RSVP with IndyPy to get the Zoom info: [https://sixfeetup.zoom.us/meeting/register/QiJIN4D8QMeULjCmI7Rftw#/registration ](https://sixfeetup.zoom.us/meeting/register/QiJIN4D8QMeULjCmI7Rftw#/registration) **About** Django just turned 21, and Python web development keeps evolving. What's changing in Django's open-source community? And how do you decide between Django and FastAPI for your next project? Join us for two talks exploring the future of Django and the real-world tradeoffs between two popular Python frameworks. Discover what's new, learn from production experience, and walk away with practical insights for your next project. Join us either in person or remotely for our hybrid event! * **IN PERSON:** E-gineering in Indianapolis, IN * **REMOTE:** [Register to get the Zoom link.](https://sixfeetup.zoom.us/meeting/register/QiJIN4D8QMeULjCmI7Rftw) **AGENDA** **7:10 - 7:25pm: Meet Your Tribe (Icebreakers)** Meet fellow Python enthusiasts, make new connections, and kick off the evening with fun icebreakers. **7:25 - 7:30pm:** Announcements **7:30 - 7:55pm: “What's New in Contributing to Django?” by Tim Schilling, Better Simple Django & Python Consultant** Django just turned 21, but there's more to celebrate than its longevity. Tim will explore how these initiatives are making Django more sustainable, welcoming, and easier to contribute to, and why its community is one of the framework's greatest strengths. **7:55 - 8:20pm: “Batteries-Included vs. Speed: The Django/FastAPI Debate” by Calvin Hendryx-Parker, Six Feet Up CTO and AWS Hero** Django or FastAPI?
